title: Graph Analytics for Telco Customer Churn Prediction
diagram:
graph LR A[Telco call data
customers + calls] --> B[01 EDA
vertices & edges] B --> C[02 Customer FE
demographics/usage] B --> D[03 Graph FE
GraphFrames: degree, pagerank] C --> E[Feature Store table] D --> E E --> F[04 AutoML.classify
MLflow tracking] F --> G[Best churn model
+ generated notebook]
preview: Telco churn modeled on the customer call network: customers as nodes and phone calls as edges. Builds graph features (degree, pagerank) with Spark GraphFrames alongside customer features, registers them in Feature Store, then trains a churn classifier with Databricks AutoML tracked in MLflow.
portfolio_value: Showcases graph-based feature engineering fused with AutoML and Feature Store in a single Databricks pipeline; strong proof of advanced ML feature design beyond tabular data.
notes: branch main. RUNME.py orchestrates a 4-step multi-task job (01 EDA -> 02 Customer FE -> 03 Graph FE -> 04 AutoML). AutoML invoked via databricks.automl.classify; features persisted with FeatureStoreClient.create_table.

requirements: Real-Time Mode cluster (DBR 18.0 LTS, Photon off)
diagram:
graph LR A[Kafka transactions] --> B[Real-Time Mode
trigger realTime] B --> C[transformWithState
per-card velocity TTL] C --> D[Dictionary enrichment

preview: End-to-end real-time fraud detection on Databricks Real-Time Mode: scores transactions in sub-300ms by training a RandomForest model in MLflow, serving it as a Spark UDF inside a Structured Streaming pipeline, with transformWithState velocity tracking, Lakebase online feature store, and a Streamlit monitoring app.
portfolio_value: Demonstrates production streaming ML: MLflow model trained and served as a Spark UDF inside a low-latency streaming pipeline, plus online feature store and live app. High-signal for real-time ML engineering.
notes: branch main. Quick Start (RTM_00) runs with zero external deps via rate source; RTM_02 adds MLflow RandomForest + Lakebase. Asset Bundle (databricks.yml) provides one-command deploy/run.

title: Databricks Fraud Framework: Two-Stage Rules + ML Orchestration
diagram:
graph LR A[Transactions Delta] --> B[01 dff_model
rules + XGBoost] B --> C[MLflow pyfunc
XGB custom model] B --> D[SHAP explainability] A --> E[02 dff_orchestration] C --> E E --> F[DMN rules engine
NetworkX topological DAG] F --> G[Fraud decision
rule URI or model URI]
preview: Two-stage fraud framework blending a rules engine with machine learning in a single orchestration layer: trains an XGBoost model with MLflow (packaged as a pyfunc custom model) and SHAP explainability, then orchestrates rules and models as a NetworkX DAG driven by a DMN ruleset.
portfolio_value: Classic decision-science pattern: combining deterministic rules with an explainable XGBoost/MLflow model in one orchestrated pipeline. Strong example of model packaging (pyfunc) and explainability for FSI.
notes: branch main. Repo is ARCHIVED (read-only) but fully legible. XGB wrapped as MLflow pyfunc custom model loaded once per orchestration; rules/models composed via nx.topological_sort over a DMN-defined DAG.

title: Geospatial Fraud Detection with GEOSCAN Clustering
diagram:
graph LR A[Card transactions
lat/lon] --> B[01 H3 indexing
geohash tiles] B --> C[GEOSCAN clustering
setPredictionCol cluster] C --> D[Per-user behaviour
tiles + tf-idf] D --> E[H3Lookup pyfunc
logged to MLflow] E --> F[02 Score new tx
normal vs anomalous] F --> G[Personalized fraud alerts]
preview: Geospatial fraud prevention at scale: uses the open-source GEOSCAN clustering algorithm over H3-indexed card transactions to learn each customer's normal spending geography, packages the lookup as an MLflow pyfunc model, then flags anomalous (out-of-pattern) transactions as personalized fraud signals.
portfolio_value: Distinctive geospatial ML angle: unsupervised clustering for personalized anomaly detection, H3 indexing, Bloom filters, and an MLflow pyfunc serving model. Stands out from tabular fraud demos.
notes: branch main (web-sync branch holds website version). GEOSCAN sets prediction column 'cluster'; H3Lookup wrapped as MLflow pyfunc and logged with mlflow.active_run. RUNME orchestrates the multi-step job.

portfolio_value: Comprehensive end-to-end supervised ML workflow: covers selection, distributed tuning, registry-based MLOps promotion, and downstream scoring/integration. Solid all-round ML engineering showcase.
notes: branch main. 5-notebook pipeline orchestrated by RUNME. XGBClassifier is best single model; Hyperopt uses SparkTrials for parallel tuning; model promoted to Production via mlflow model registry, scored as pyfunc for CRM export.

title: Survival Analysis for Churn & Customer Lifetime Value
diagram:
graph LR A[Customer tenure
+ churn event] --> B[02 Kaplan-Meier
survival curves] A --> C[03 Cox PH
covariate hazards] A --> D[04 AFT
Weibull/LogNormal/LogLogistic] C --> E[Survival probability
per cohort] D --> E E --> F[05 Customer Lifetime Value
expected profit + NPV]
preview: Statistical time-to-event modeling for customer attrition and lifetime value using the lifelines library: Kaplan-Meier survival curves, Cox Proportional Hazards regression, and Accelerated Failure Time models (Weibull / LogNormal / LogLogistic), then converts survival probabilities into expected monthly profit and NPV-based customer lifetime value.
portfolio_value: Demonstrates the statistical-ML branch of churn modeling (survival/hazard) plus a clean translation of model output into business value (CLV/NPV). Complements classification-based churn work.
notes: branch main. 6-notebook pipeline via RUNME. Uses lifelines (KaplanMeierFitter, CoxPHFitter, Weibull/LogNormal/LogLogistic AFT fitters) incl. proportional-hazard and pairwise log-rank assumption tests; CLV derived from cph.predict_survival_function.
